items.definition:
to have an unfavorable opinion
Her parents disapprove of her new boyfriend.

to leave one's own country to settle permanently in another
Many people emigrate for better job opportunities.

make a deep, inarticulate sound in response to pain or despair
He let out a groan of pain.

to breathe out
Take a deep breath in, then slowly exhale.

to change the time or date of something
We had to reschedule the meeting due to a conflict.

to utter a prolonged, mournful cry
The baby began to wail loudly.

to take or move (someone or something) in a particular direction suddenly and quickly
She whisked the eggs for the omelet.

become too hot
The car engine started to overheat.

To make or keep cold or cool.
Please refrigerate the leftovers to keep them fresh.

to feel a slight prickling or stinging sensation
My fingers began to tingle from the cold.

to draw a line under; to emphasize
Please underline the main points in the text.

To eat (something) steadily and often audibly.
The rabbit munched on a carrot.

To marry again.
After her divorce, she decided to remarry.

to let liquid fall in small drops; to move a ball by short kicks or bounces
The baby started to dribble milk down his chin.

to move with quick, light, irregular motions
The butterflies began to flutter their wings as the sun came out.

to make the characteristic harsh sound of a duck
The duck began to quack loudly as we approached.

pack or store (an object) carefully and neatly in a particular place.
Please stow your luggage in the overhead compartment.

feel or express sympathy.
I sympathize with your difficult situation.

let saliva flow from the mouth
The baby started to drool when he saw the bottle.

cry out suddenly in surprise, anger, or excitement
She would often exclaim with delight when she saw her grandchildren.

make a sharp, sibilant sound as of the letter s
The snake began to hiss loudly.

to treat (a person or animal) badly
It's wrong to mistreat animals.

to turn from liquid into vapor
The water will evaporate quickly in the sun.

to change the structure or form of something
They decided to remodel their kitchen.

snuggle (to settle or move into a warm, comfortable position)
The children loved to snuggle with their dog on the sofa.

To order (something) before it is available.
You can preorder the new game now.

to injure a joint by twisting it
She managed to sprain her ankle while hiking.

to cut up or grind (food, especially meat) into very small pieces
Please mince the garlic finely for the sauce.

to move unsteadily from side to side
The table began to wobble when he leaned on it.

appear again
After a long absence, the sun finally reappeared from behind the clouds.

change the position or arrangement of something
She decided to rearrange the furniture in her living room.

To jump from an aircraft and fall freely before opening a parachute
She decided to skydive for her 30th birthday.

To make a sudden sound through the nose
The horse gave a loud snort.

To make or become sweet or sweeter
You can sweeten your tea with honey.

to make someone work too hard
He tends to overwork himself before deadlines.

to organize (something) again in a different way
The company decided to reorganize its departments.

to read (something) again
I often reread my favorite books.

make or become black
The smoke began to blacken the walls.

To spell (a word) incorrectly.
It's easy to misspell 'receive' or 'believe'.

to discover again
She hopes to rediscover her passion for painting.

to steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer
She was caught trying to shoplift a dress.

To read incorrectly.
I think I misread the instructions, so the cake didn't turn out right.

to rebuke angrily
She would often scold her children for misbehaving.

make a loud, harsh sound (like a goose or car horn)
The driver had to honk his horn to warn the pedestrian.

to tell again
She asked him to retell the story from the beginning.

to cut with a saw
He used a hacksaw to saw through the metal pipe.

to swallow quickly or in large mouthfuls
He gulped down his water after the run.

to come to live permanently in a foreign country
Many people immigrate to new countries for better opportunities.

to supply with more fuel
The plane needed to refuel before continuing its long journey.

to sell something again
Many people buy concert tickets just to resell them at a higher price.

to produce an idea or way of solving a problem by holding a spontaneous group discussion
Let's brainstorm some ideas for the new marketing campaign.

To move making a regular muffled explosive sound, as of a steam engine or motorboat.
The old train began to chug slowly up the hill.

ask for information from someone
I need to enquire about the train schedule.

To let air or gas out of (a tire, balloon, or similar inflatable object).
The mechanic had to deflate the tire to repair it.

to pay too much for something
Be careful not to overpay for that used car.

to heat (an oven or other cooking appliance) to a specified temperature before putting food in it
Remember to preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius.

to complain in a bad-tempered way
He continued to grumble about the cold weather.

To make or become longer.
The tailor had to lengthen the trousers.

To score more points than an opponent.
Our team managed to outscore the opposition in the final quarter.

to make or become thick or thicker
You can thicken the sauce by adding a little cornstarch.

to make a short, sharp, high-pitched sound
The birds began to chirp as the sun rose.

to utter a high-pitched scream
She let out a shriek of terror when she saw the spider.

to make or become fresh
She opened the window to freshen the air in the room.

To take small bites
The rabbit began to nibble on the carrot.
